paragraphs.text: Vickers Wellington B Mk X LN775 was lost on 1 March 1944. It belonged to 3 Overseas Aircraft Dispatch Unit at RAF Hurn, Dorset, and was on a transfer flight to Mediterranean Air Command at Rabat, Morocco. It drifted about 25 miles off the briefed route and flew into the hillside at Three Barrows Hill on Dartmoor in cloud. All four crew were killed. Dartmoor Explorations names them as Pilot Officer Frederick Cooke, Flight Sergeants William Jack and Alfred Beeston, and Sergeant John Yeates. Their roles, ages, service numbers and burial places are not yet confirmed from CWGC or IBCC.
A temporary memorial at the site lists the four crew. No source found says who looks after it.

notes: Single researched source for everything. No IWM War Memorials Register entry found by search. Legendary Dartmoor page (cited in our record) returned HTTP 500 twice, so unread. Crew names could not be matched to CWGC or IBCC: searches returned only different men (e.g. Sgt John Yates, 38 Sqn, died 1944-03-01, Alamein Memorial, is a different unit and almost certainly not our Yeates). OADU ferry units may not appear in IBCC. Our record says squadron 'Bomber Command' and 'Dartmoor National Park Authority' as maintainer; neither is supported by S1. S1 says the memorial is temporary, so a maintainer is unlikely to be the National Park Authority without a source. Another search summary suggested the page mixed in a 1941 Hameldown crew list; a direct re-read showed the names sit under the LN775 memorial caption, with Hameldown mentioned only as a comparison site. Warmemorialsonline/tracesofwar/baaa-acro pages for this crash were blocked (403) or unrelated.
